item.title: 🟠 New 7-Zip Vulnerability Could Let Crafted XZ Archives Run Code During Extraction
item.description:
Why this matters: Leadership context — useful for risk, budget, and vendor conversations.
Opening a crafted XZ archive in 7-Zip could let an attacker run code on the machine. The flaw, CVE-2026-14266, is a heap-based buffer overflow in how the archiver processes XZ chunked data, and Trend Micro's Zero Day Initiative (ZDI) detailed it on July 15. A fix shipped on June 25 in 7-Zip 26.02. The overflow lets an attacker "execute code in the context of the current process," per the

item.title: 🟠 OpenSSL HollowByte Flaw Could Freeze Server Memory with 11-Byte TLS Requests
item.description:
Why this matters: Leadership context — useful for risk, budget, and vendor conversations.
Eleven bytes will make an unpatched OpenSSL server set aside up to 131 KB of memory for a message that never arrives. On the glibc systems Okta tested, that memory is gone until the process restarts.
